analysis:
In the Union Budget 2024-25 speech, the Finance Minister announced PM Awas Yojana-Urban 2.0 for one crore urban poor and middle-class families, with an investment of ₹10 lakh crore and central assistance of ₹2.2 lakh crore over five years. The Union Cabinet formally approved the scheme on 9 August 2024, and MoHUA records it as effective from 1 September 2024.

MoHUA sanction data reported by DD India show that total houses sanctioned under PMAY-U 2.0 reached about 20.80 lakh by October 2026, against the one-crore target. A PIB release of 15 October 2025 recorded 1.41 lakh additional houses sanctioned at the fifth CSMC meeting.

The five-year implementation window runs from 2024, so the target is still open.
notes: This is a distinct promise from the earlier 'Housing for All by 2022' commitment (modi-2017-housing-for-all-by-2022): it is a new scheme (PMAY-U 2.0) with a new one-crore target and a 2024-2029 window. The ₹2.2 lakh crore figure is used in the Budget speech while the PMO/moHUA pages cite ₹2.30 lakh crore government assistance; both appear in official material.
